ideation.icp_description: B2B companies (all-sector, per user decision 2026-05-27), 100-1000 employees, HQ in US or UK, direct employers, that are HIRING a Sales Enablement / Revenue Enablement / RevOps / Sales Operations role. The hire signals the company is staffing or expanding the function that owns the sales tech stack and rep adoption of it.
ideation.offer: Arnic increases adoption of tools among a company's employees — i.e. gets the sales team to actually USE the sales stack they've bought (CRM, sales engagement, enablement tooling) instead of it sitting unused. The person we email is the Head of Sales / VP Sales / CRO who owns the number and feels the pain of low tool adoption.
ideation.why_signal_fits: When a company hires a RevOps / Sales-Ops / Sales-Enablement person, it is investing in the exact function that owns CRM + sales-tool rollout and rep adoption. That hire is the clearest in-market signal that (a) they have a sales stack worth adopting, and (b) they are actively trying to drive adoption of it. Arnic accelerates that adoption so the tooling investment pays off.

qualification._status: CONFIRMED 2026-05-28 (user feedback on first data-processing run). Any sales-operations-related role qualifies regardless of IC vs management level; geography is NOT a qualification gate; sub-100-employee rows are excluded at processing.
qualification._purpose: Role-only judgement layer applied by lilly-theirstack-data-processing Phase 2.5. Classifies each new Jobs row QUALIFIED / BORDERLINE / OFF_BRIEF on whether the role is sales-operations-related (RevOps / Sales Ops / Sales-Enablement / Revenue-Enablement). Never excludes companies — only roles. Geography is NOT used here. The sub-100-employee exclusion is a separate processing gate, not a role verdict.
qualification.role_signal_definition: The new hire will own, run, or directly support the company's sales tech stack and the sales team's adoption of it (RevOps, Sales Ops, Sales/Revenue Enablement) — at ANY level, IC Analyst/Specialist included. The function (sales-operations-related) is what qualifies, not the seniority. Not a marketing-ops role, not a software engineer building an internal tool, not a generic operations generalist.
qualified_role_patterns: Sales Enablement / Revenue Enablement — any level: Specialist / Analyst / Coordinator-IC / Manager / Senior Manager / Lead / Director / Head / VP
Revenue Operations / RevOps — any level: Analyst / Specialist / Manager / Lead / Director / Head / VP

Sales Operations / Sales Ops — any level: Analyst / Specialist / Manager / Lead / Director / Head / VP (incl. CRM Sales-Ops Analyst, Retail/Channel Sales-Ops, Sales-Ops within an ad/retail-media partnership role)
GTM Operations / Go-to-Market Operations (sales-led) — any level

_RULE 2026-05-28: any sales-operations-related role is QUALIFIED, IC analysts/specialists included. Per user: 'all the borderlines are actually permitted, because they're sales operations related roles.'
disqualified_role_patterns: Marketing Operations / Marketing Ops — owns the marketing stack, not the sales stack
Business Operations / BizOps / Strategy & Ops — generalist, not sales-tool owner
Salesforce Developer / CRM Developer / RevOps Engineer (software build) — engineer building tooling, not driving rep adoption
Customer Success Operations / CS Ops — retention stack, not new-logo sales stack
Partner / Channel Operations (pure) — partner motion, not direct sales adoption
Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (S&OP) / demand planning — supply-chain, not sales tech stack
Generic operations leadership with no Sales/Revenue/Enablement function (e.g. 'Campus Operations', plain 'Operations Director') — not sales-ops
Intern / Associate / Coordinator level — STILL disqualified by default (no system or adoption ownership); revisit with user if a borderline sales-ops coordinator looks like a first dedicated hire
borderline_role_patterns: Operations Manager (no Sales/Revenue/Enablement prefix) — could be sales-ops or generic ops; needs context
Revenue Operations leaning Marketing (title mixes both) — check which stack dominates

Role.instructions: Direct lookup from the Jobs row 'Job Title', NORMALISED so it reads naturally after the hardcoded hook 'Saw you're hiring a ___'. Rules: (1) replace a comma separating a level word from a function area with ' of ' so 'Director, Revenue Operations' becomes 'Director of Revenue Operations'; (2) drop bracketed/parenthetical or trailing geographic qualifiers so 'RevOps Manager (Remote)' becomes 'RevOps Manager' and 'Account Executive - France & Southern Europe' becomes 'Account Executive'; (3) trim whitespace; (4) preserve seniority words (Senior, Director, Manager, Head, VP, Lead, Chief). No LLM call needed for (1)-(3); escalate only if genuinely ambiguous.
Role.validation: Non-empty. Reads naturally after 'Saw you're hiring a ___'. No comma in the level/function position, no parentheses, no trailing geographic qualifier.
